text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing its behavior. The main goal is to make the code easier to read, understand, and maintain. Developers often rewrite messy sections, remove duplication, and rename variables so the logic becomes clearer. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should work exactly as before. It is also a powerful way to reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor design choices accumulate over time. By refactoring regularly, teams keep their code clean and make future changes faster and safer.
